facts.fact: The authors, from 37 interviews in May and June 2019, state that facilities aggregate patient data each month onto paper reports and submit them to district health offices, where information officers key them into DHIS2; some larger health centres and hospitals aggregate electronically before submitting to the district office.
facts.system: Health Management Information System (HMIS) on DHIS2

facts.fact: The paper describes the HMIS as collecting monthly reports from all facilities under the districts: rural health posts, rural and urban health centres, and district and provincial hospitals, with up to 21 paper registers in smaller facilities and 25 in some district hospitals and the provincial hospital at the time of the 2019 interviews; entry into DHIS2 is at the district office, not at these facilities.
facts.system: Health Management Information System (HMIS) on DHIS2

facts.fact: The paper gives no count or share of facilities entering their own reports; it describes staff of remote Western Province facilities carrying monthly paper reports to the district office, up to 170 km away, by motorbike, canoe or ox cart, on fieldwork of May and June 2019.
facts.system: Health Management Information System (HMIS) on DHIS2

facts.fact: The paper states that the HMIS is managed by the central Ministry of Health, which oversaw its revamping on the DHIS2 platform after health authority was re-centralised from 2006; interviews of May and June 2019.
facts.system: Health Management Information System (HMIS) on DHIS2

facts.fact: The paper states that the development and strengthening of the HMIS were historically largely driven by donor support, and a district respondent reports Global Fund support for retraining staff on new HMIS tools in 2018; it names no domestic budget line; interviews of May and June 2019.
facts.system: Health Management Information System (HMIS) on DHIS2

facts.fact: The paper states that within some larger health centres and hospitals data are collected digitally through the electronic health record system 'when possible', and that the record system was implemented in select districts; elsewhere patient history is written in paper 'passports' carried by the patient; interviews of May and June 2019.

The paper states that although SmartCare was introduced more than ten years earlier, most facilities in Western Province had not been able to switch from the paper-based system for lack of computers, steady power, internet and funds for the software and hardware; it gives no count; interviews of May and June 2019, one province only.

The paper states that the Ministry of Health has been implementing SmartCare, an electronic health record system giving patients a digitised health passport, and that the ministry developed it in partnership with the US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention; interviews of May and June 2019.

systems.tiers: health posts, health centres, district and provincial hospitals report on paper; keyed at district health offices; viewable at provincial and national level

systems.platform: developed by the Ministry of Health with US CDC
